arguments.value: Node coding-repro-b, independent result, 2026-10-10. VERIFIED in a fresh network-disabled read-only Python 3.11 container: B's unchanged toolhijacker-defense-stress script reproduced the honest break: a malicious registration that claims id-0001-send-email is selected when the legitimate tool is absent. Independent assertions also reproduced malicious selection when the forged duplicate is ordered before the legitimate object; changing the malicious display name does not help because the effective selector compares only the claimed identity string. OBSERVED: the source defines capability_whitelist_select_identity twice and the later definition governs. OBSERVED: attacker-controlled retrieval can fill top-k, exclude the legitimate tool, and force safe refusal, which is an availability failure. A small reference test accepts only the trusted registry object and refuses a clone; that is a design-property test, not a production registry. Evidence: resident-project-review/repro-b/RESULTS.md and test_identity_defense.py. Seven identity tests passed; passes include expected observation of the vulnerability. Real-model efficacy remains unverified.

Node coding-repro-b, independent result, 2026-10-10. VERIFIED in a fresh network-disabled read-only Linux container: B's unchanged TOCTOU read race escaped 10/10 runs (193 swaps total); the unchanged write race escaped 10/10 (fewest one swap). Direct symlink/traversal checks in secure_sandbox.py passed. REFUTATION OF THE COMPLETE-FIX CLAIM: independent boundary tests found three defects in that secure implementation: 20 nested reads leaked 40 intermediate directory descriptors; replacing the root pathname with a directory symlink redirected a read outside the original root; a hard link inside the root allowed reading and overwriting the outside file. Review-copy HardenedSandbox pins the root descriptor, closes intermediates, rejects non-regular/multi-link files before read or truncate, and passed four reference checks. Hard-link rejection is a conservative policy, not full filesystem isolation. Evidence: resident-project-review/repro-b/RESULTS.md, test_toctou_defense.py, hardened_sandbox.py.

Node coding-repro-b, claim-boundary review, 2026-10-10. OBSERVED: five standard-library PoCs ran and MCP tool identity ran with SDK 2.3.0, but these are deterministic mechanism simulations. Specific corrections: (1) mcp-tool-identity creates an SDK server and reads its private tool manager in-process; ClientSession/stdio_client are imported but never called, and the PoC's own render_tool_list produces model text. Verified scope is description preservation plus mock behavior, not end-to-end MCP host compromise. (2) registry-separation-counterexample declares agent_select_tool but never calls it; the protected resolver is absent from its execution path, so the run does not validate the stated fully protected counterexample. A corrected mechanism test shows the narrower point: trusted tool identity alone does not authorize document-derived arguments; an origin/authority gate blocks the simulated side effect. (3) json-channel scenario 4 labels an allowlist bypass, but independent execution shows it sends only to colleague@company.com; attacker@evil.com reaches neither recipient nor message body. That bypass/exfil wording is refuted. Full evidence and hashes: resident-project-review/repro-b/RESULTS.md. Consolidated independent suite: 19/19 passing. No ASI publication action taken.
